acceptance_matrix.requirement: Freeze one approved expected-ID fixture for the world, five employer city definitions, exactly five employer capital instances, every approved project, every visible skill definition, every employer-skill instance, every project-skill link, every factual evidence reference, and each visible asset's selected canonical trace-panel metadata plus code-native master geometry identity. Employer anchors are non-visible district/camera coordinates, not asset instances.
acceptance_matrix.pass: IDs and versions are unique; exactly one world exists; each of the five employers has exactly one capital instance whose kind is capital and whose assetId exactly equals that employer's canonical city asset; the registry has zero kind:city instances; no city/capital visual or transform is rendered directly from an employer anchor; instance/ninjaone/capital/01 remains at local (420, 500) and derived world position (316.08, 366.88); the other four final capital positions are fixed only after a recorded footprint/collision review and all five final positions pass collision review before CW-007; each project has exactly one project asset; each employer-skill pair has zero or one instance; every link resolves; every visible runtime asset has one selected trace-panel ID/SHA and accepted geometryKey, masterGeometryHash, primaryPathHash, footprint, orientation, and projection ID; actual IDs equal the Director-approved expected inventory with no extras or omissions.
acceptance_matrix.fail: Capital count is not exactly five; an employer has zero or multiple capitals; a capital does not use its employer's city asset; any kind:city instance or direct anchor-derived city/capital visual exists; the NinjaOne capital tuple drifts; a final capital position lacks collision review or overlaps an accepted footprint/route/interaction clearance; any duplicate, dangling reference, missing/extra expected ID, visible runtime asset without selected-panel metadata or accepted code-native geometry identity, duplicate employer-skill instance, or unresolved evidence reference.

acceptance_matrix.requirement: Across overview, employer, project, and summary states, preserve each instance identity tuple exactly: assetId, version, geometryKey, masterGeometryHash, primaryPathHash, footprint, orientation, worldPosition, city ownership, and authored projection ID.
acceptance_matrix.pass: Deep equality succeeds for every tuple at every state; the exact code-native master geometry and primary-path hashes are unchanged; only camera x/y/scale, focus/emphasis, and declared interior-detail visibility differ. Browser instrumentation reports no instance remount, geometry substitution, or coordinate mutation caused by zoom.
acceptance_matrix.fail: Any regenerated ID, changed coordinates, footprint, orientation, master geometry/path hash, ownership, projection, geometry substitution, or state-specific duplicate.

acceptance_matrix.requirement: Each asset records one selected canonical trace panel, and every runtime LOD derives from one code-native master footprint, primary silhouette, orientation, roofline, facade rhythm, sign slot, and projection identity. Lower LODs may hide interior-detail groups only.
acceptance_matrix.pass: The selected panel ID/SHA is recorded as a non-runtime art/identity reference; the code-native masterGeometryHash and primaryPathHash are exact matches across every zoom/LOD state; LOD instrumentation shows only declared interior-detail group visibility changing; the reviewer confirms the rendered identity and projection remain recognizable without using AI-sheet cross-panel parity as proof.
acceptance_matrix.fail: Missing selected trace panel, changed runtime master geometry/path hash, footprint, orientation, projection, roofline, or silhouette; an LOD redraws/substitutes the asset or changes primary masses; hidden detail is not explicitly declared; or reviewer evidence is absent.

acceptance_matrix.requirement: Opening and closing a project summary drawer occludes the exact project-focus map without reflowing, recentering, panning, zooming, regenerating, or losing selection.
acceptance_matrix.pass: Before-open, open, and after-close snapshots are deeply equal for camera x/y/scale, focusedProject, selected links, and every asset transform; the same map DOM/root instance remains; visual diff outside the drawer mask is zero except declared animated ambience.
acceptance_matrix.fail: Any state drift, remount, artwork swap, layout reflow, clipped required target, or unexplained pixel change outside the overlay mask.

acceptance_matrix.requirement: All world, city, project, and skill assets use one accepted orthographic top-down/isometric projection with one azimuth, elevation, north direction, and non-rotatable authored composition.
acceptance_matrix.pass: Every code-native asset and instance references the same accepted projection ID and exact camera metadata; deterministic axis/north checks align; the selected canonical trace panel for each asset is reviewed for compatible projection/style, and runtime screenshots show no perspective, rotation, or projection drift.
acceptance_matrix.fail: Missing or unequal projection metadata, free authored rotation, mismatched north, perspective drift, or absent reviewer verdict.

acceptance_matrix.requirement: Every instance of a skill reuses the same code-native canonical geometry and silhouette; employer variants may change only palette slots and city placement.
acceptance_matrix.pass: For each skill and LOD, the geometryKey, masterGeometryHash, primaryPathHash, footprint, roofline, facade rhythm, sign slot, orientation, and projection ID are exact matches across employers and zoom states; all eight required palette slots resolve and no employer-specific baked color or geometry exists.
acceptance_matrix.fail: Any employer-specific geometry, unequal code-native geometry/path hash or primary silhouette identity, missing slot, duplicate same-city instance, project-specific skill clone, baked employer color, or concept-sheet panel used as the comparison authority.

acceptance_matrix.requirement: Each project has one unique accepted code-native landmark, one selected canonical trace panel, and a stable recognizable identity across zoom states within the restrained technical-cartography language.
acceptance_matrix.pass: Every project records one non-runtime selected trace-panel ID/SHA and one accepted code-native geometry identity; exact master geometry/primary-path hashes persist across zoom while only interior detail visibility changes; runtime screenshots retain the selected panel's identity, near-black field, desaturated contours, thin isometric strokes, limited emissive accents, tracked labels, and low bloom without photorealistic or graph/dashboard drift; concept PNGs are not shipped or requested by the runtime.

acceptance_matrix.requirement: Ambient vehicles, packets, people, machinery, and stack easter eggs remain restrained entertainment-only decoration.
acceptance_matrix.pass: Every ambient item is inventoried as illustrative, excluded from evidence/outcome fields, does not alter canonical geometry, does not obscure a label/focus ring/touch target at any required viewport, is aria-hidden when non-interactive, and receives an explicit reviewer pass for visual hierarchy.
acceptance_matrix.fail: An ambient item implies a measured outcome, populates evidence, becomes required navigation, changes a canonical silhouette, dominates the project landmark, obscures interaction, or adds noisy accessibility output.

acceptance_matrix.requirement: Every world/city/project visual state exposes a visible and screen-reader-readable disclosure that the scene is illustrative and that visual scale/activity are not measured outcomes.

acceptance_matrix.fail: Missing, hidden, low-contrast, visually ambiguous, repeated/noisy, or inaccessible disclosure; or copy that labels only some visual states.

acceptance_matrix.requirement: Every currently interactive city, project, skill, map control, and inspector action has equivalent pointer and keyboard paths.
acceptance_matrix.pass: Pointer click and keyboard Enter/Space produce the same selected ID and camera/state result; Tab or an explicitly documented roving-arrow pattern reaches every visible target; zoom out/reset/in controls work by keyboard; Escape closes overlays; no action requires hover or wheel alone.
acceptance_matrix.fail: Unreachable target, divergent state, hover/wheel-only action, keyboard trap, unexpected page scroll, or an activation that changes the wrong asset/state.

acceptance_matrix.requirement: On the phone viewport and one physical touch device, tap activates cities/projects/skills, one-finger drag pans without accidental activation, visible controls provide map zoom without requiring wheel/pinch, and browser page zoom remains available.
acceptance_matrix.pass: Emulated and physical-device tap/drag traces produce the expected state; drag threshold prevents accidental opens; all interactive targets are at least 44 by 44 CSS pixels; browser navigation, document scroll outside the map, and browser pinch/page zoom remain usable; overlay actions remain reachable above safe-area insets.
acceptance_matrix.fail: Tap miss, accidental activation while panning, target below 44 by 44, trapped page or browser-zoom gesture, required pinch/wheel path for map navigation, or obscured action.

acceptance_matrix.requirement: The accepted overlay contract explicitly declares modal or non-modal semantics. Focus is visible, moves to the project-summary heading after open, follows a logical order through visible controls, never lands on obscured/inert map targets, and returns to the exact invoking target after close or Escape.
acceptance_matrix.pass: Recorded activeElement transitions match the invoking target ID; the heading receives programmatic focus; focus indicators remain visible in default and forced-colors modes. A modal overlay exposes dialog semantics, contains focus, and makes the background inert. A non-modal overlay leaves only visible, unobscured background targets reachable. No focus loss, accidental trap, or behind-drawer focus occurs.
acceptance_matrix.fail: Focus resets to body, moves to a different asset, enters hidden/obscured content, lacks a visible ring, becomes trapped, or fails to return.

acceptance_matrix.requirement: prefers-reduced-motion removes nonessential camera interpolation, particles, ambient loops, parallax, and overlay animation without removing information or blocking navigation, including when the preference changes while the page is open.
acceptance_matrix.pass: With reduced motion emulated before load, state changes complete in one frame or a near-zero CSS duration; no continuous requestAnimationFrame loop changes pixels; all IDs, labels, and actions remain available; no autoplay begins. Switching the preference during an active transition or ambient loop stops nonessential motion without state loss.
acceptance_matrix.fail: Residual looping motion, animated camera travel, lost content/action, delayed completion, autoplay, or preference read only after motion starts.

acceptance_matrix.requirement: At 1440x900, 900x900, 390x844, breakpoint pairs 600/601 and 940/941 pixels, landscape phone, and 200/400 percent browser zoom, canonical world coordinates stay fixed while camera framing and responsive overlay dimensions keep required labels and actions usable.
acceptance_matrix.pass: Registry coordinates remain identical; no two-dimensional page scrolling is required to read factual content at 400 percent; no horizontal page overflow traps input; no interactive target or focus ring is clipped; drawer and safe-area layout are usable; screenshot reviewer records no overlap that changes meaning or blocks input.
acceptance_matrix.fail: Responsive recomputation changes world coordinates, required content clips/overlaps, horizontal overflow traps input, or a target becomes unreachable.

acceptance_matrix.requirement: Run Axe and WAVE against the immutable preview in overview, representative city, representative project focus, and open-overlay states at desktop and phone sizes; deduplicate by rule plus element and manually adjudicate disagreements.
acceptance_matrix.pass: Zero unresolved Axe critical/serious violations; zero WAVE errors or contrast errors; all alerts and tool disagreements have selector, WCAG mapping, confidence, reviewer disposition, and validation note; hidden states are scanned after activation.
acceptance_matrix.fail: Any unresolved critical/serious/error/contrast finding, missing raw export, unscanned activated state, selector-less issue, or tool disagreement silently discarded.

acceptance_matrix.requirement: Canvas or other visual-only rendering is decorative to assistive technology; every interactive city, project, skill, state, and map control has an equivalent semantic DOM control or region with an accurate accessible name, role, and state.
acceptance_matrix.pass: Visual-only layers are aria-hidden; no interactive target exists only in pixels; the semantic control count and IDs equal the interactive registry; selected, focused, disabled, expanded, and current states are exposed; screen-reader activation produces the same state as pointer activation.
acceptance_matrix.fail: Meaningful canvas content has no semantic equivalent, duplicate visual and semantic announcements occur, DOM controls omit or misstate registry items/state, or assistive activation diverges from pointer activation.

acceptance_matrix.requirement: Manually validate the complete keyboard path, accessible names/roles/states, focus order/restoration, illustration disclosure, live status behavior, overlay reading order, and forced-colors focus/selection cues.
acceptance_matrix.pass: No core path is keyboard-blocked; controls expose accurate name/role/value/state; the map and overlay have unique labels; one screen-reader smoke run announces the selected asset, disclosure, heading, and close result without duplicate decorative output; forced-colors preserves state without color alone.
acceptance_matrix.fail: Keyboard blocker, unlabeled or mislabeled action, missing state, incorrect reading order, disclosure not announced, decorative noise, or selection/focus conveyed only by color.

acceptance_matrix.requirement: The 2D Career World remains lightweight, responsive, and usable without WebGL/WebGPU before any 3D implementation begins.

Engine choice may remain a separate promoted technical decision.

acceptance_matrix.requirement: After CW-008 implementation, verify the 3D engine and model are requested only after explicit activation and that initial 2D budgets remain green.
acceptance_matrix.pass: Pre-activation HAR contains zero 3D requests; the request begins only after activation; returning to 2D preserves the exact prior state; CW7-PERF-001 reruns green; the 3D performance budgets promoted for CW-009 all pass.
acceptance_matrix.fail: Eager/prefetched 3D bytes, initial budget regression, 2D state loss, or any promoted 3D budget failure.

acceptance_matrix.requirement: After CW-008 implementation, verify unsupported graphics, dynamic-import rejection, model-load rejection, and timeout fallbacks.
acceptance_matrix.pass: Each injected failure retains the 2D state, surfaces a named accessible error/status within one second of the failure decision, offers working retry and return actions, and produces zero uncaught errors or data loss.
acceptance_matrix.fail: Blank screen, lost 2D state, inaccessible or missing error, broken retry/return, uncaught rejection, or data loss.
